title: Quiz: State Classification — Recurrence, Transience, and Ergodicity

questions.text: State j is 'accessible' from state i (written i → j) if:
options: P^(n)_{ij} > 0 for some n ≥ 0 (positive probability of reaching j from i in some number of steps)
States i and j are in the same communicating class
The chain visits i and j with equal long-run frequency
questions.explanation: Accessibility (i → j) only requires that there EXISTS some n ≥ 0 for which the n-step probability P^(n)_{ij} > 0. This n does not have to be 1 — you may need multiple steps. When n=0, we have i → i trivially.

questions.text: A state with a positive self-loop probability (P_{ii} > 0) is guaranteed to be aperiodic (period = 1).
questions.explanation: If P_{ii} > 0, then the chain can return to state i in exactly 1 step. Therefore 1 ∈ {n ≥ 1 : P^(n)_{ii} > 0}, and gcd of a set containing 1 is always 1. So d(i) = gcd{1,...} = 1, meaning i is aperiodic.

questions.text: A Markov chain is called 'ergodic' if it satisfies which combination of properties?
options: Aperiodic and positive recurrent, but not necessarily irreducible
It has a unique stationary distribution
questions.explanation: Ergodicity requires all three: (1) irreducible — all states communicate; (2) aperiodic — period 1 for all states; (3) positive recurrent — finite mean return times. For finite state spaces, irreducibility implies positive recurrence, so in practice ergodic = irreducible + aperiodic for finite chains.

questions.text: The ergodic theorem says that for an ergodic chain, the long-run fraction of time spent in state i (time average) converges to:
questions.explanation: The ergodic theorem states that (1/n) Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} 1[X_k=i] → πᵢ with probability 1. The long-run time average in state i equals the stationary probability πᵢ — this is the 'time average = space average' principle.

questions.text: In a chain with an absorbing state D (P_{DD}=1), the non-absorbing states are:
options: Recurrent — because the chain can return to them infinitely often
Transient — because once the chain enters D, it never returns to the non-absorbing states
Periodic — because the chain can only revisit them at regular intervals
Null recurrent — because the mean return time is infinite
questions.explanation: Non-absorbing states that can reach the absorbing state D are transient. From any such state, there is a positive probability of entering D and never returning. The total number of visits to each transient state is finite almost surely.

questions.text: All states within the same communicating class must have the same period.
questions.explanation: Period is a class property: if i ↔ j (they communicate), then d(i) = d(j). This follows because paths from i to j and back 'interleave' with return paths to i, forcing the same gcd structure. So we can speak of the period of a communicating class, not just individual states.
